column1: # Every row says: the pin at `doc` that resolves to `target` must have
# `keyword` on the cited line. The check verifies the CONTENT, not the
# number: a row whose cited line no longer holds the keyword is a finding
# (that is the point), and a row that matches no pin is STALE-MAP.
# `target` is repo-relative and resolved (module-relative doc pins were
# resolved by the check); a map row matches a range pin when the path and
# the first line match, so re-ranging does not orphan the row.
# This is the seed inventory, not the whole corpus: the blocking flip
# (issue #787) keeps every finding that is not explicitly allow-listed in
# script/doc-pin-allowlist.tsv. These rooms rows are the live drift the
# issue records on master; each cited line had slid onto a different
# construct, and an existence-only check would pass all of them. They are
# re-pinned by content (grep, never offset arithmetic) so they enforce the
# #638 Admin fail-closed boot testing spec (issue #638). The section-2
# as-built pins, the bundle/pre-flight/Ansible/CI pins, and the guard
# traceability re-pins all resolve to a line whose content is asserted
# here, so a base move (the #788 ci.yml insert) is a finding, not a pass.
